newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - October 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - October 14.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
FINANCIAL TIMES
-- BARING BROTHERS LURES TOP BUSINESS CONSULTANT

Baring Brothers is to appoint Peter Foy, one of the UK's most influential management consultants, as its new chairman. The appointment signals the success of the Baring Brothers corporate finance business since the collapse of its parent bank last year. Foy will help Baring Brothers establish new links with large companies and win assignments to advise them on mergers, acquisitions and financing.
-- BRUSSELS BOOST FOR MARS IN ICE CREAM ROW WITH UNILEVER

The European Commission is expected to give a boost this week to efforts by confectionery company Mars to weaken the leading position which rival Unilever holds in the European ice cream market, which is worth 15 billion sterling a year. The EC is to renew its attack on Unilever over the company's practice of lending freezers to retailers which stock its ice cream products. The EC has expressed concern about the practice in Ireland, which has a large number of small retailers.
-- MORE DEFENCE PROJECTS MAY BE AWARDED TO PRIVATE SECTOR

The Ministry of Defence is looking at new ways in which the government's Private Finance Initiative (PFI) can be applied to its operations. The ministry's chief of defence procurement, Sir Robert Walmsley, has begun a review to identify military support operations which could be contracted out to the private sector under the PFI. Transport services, catering, and the repair and maintenance of weapons are all areas under consideration.
-- BARCLAYS LINKS UP WITH MICROSOFT

Barclays Bank, one of the UK's "big four" high street banks, is to link its computer-banking services with Microsoft's Money 97 personal-finance software. Barclays is the first UK bank to cooperate with Microsoft over the software, which will go on sale in November packaged with a Barclays logo and containing information on Barclays bank accounts. Barclays intends launching its PC banking service next spring.
-- KPMG WIDENS SPLIT WITH RIVALS

KMPG, one of the so-called "Big Six" British accountancy firms, is to publish a privately-commissioned poll which reveals that the directors of some of Britain's top companies want their auditors to publish full results. KPMG is the only one of the "Big Six" to publish full financial reports following its decision to incorporate its audit business.
-- COMPANIES TOLD TO GET MORE OUT OF EMPLOYEES

A report from consultants Coopers & Lybrand and the government-sponsored programme Investors In People UK, has warned that companies are failing to get the best out of their employees. The survey found that only one quarter of company employees believed they were fully involved and valued by the firm, yet 80 percent of chief executives in the companies surveyed believed they were successful in making employees aware of their overall business strategies and the contribution they could make individually.
-- SOUTHERN WATER TO CUT BACK OVERSEAS

Regional water company Southern Water, which was taken over this summer by Scottish Power in a deal worth 1.67 billion sterling, is to scale down its overseas ventures. The move, part of a shift towards focusing on the core utility business, is believed to be the outcome of a three-month review of Southern by a new management team installed by the company's new owners. Southern is negotiating a withdrawal from a joint venture in the Philippines, and will abandon a bid to operate a water-supply project in Oman.
-- SMART CAR FORECASTS QUERIED BY REPORT

A research report from MarketScope, the equity research arm of Standard & Poor's business information group, has cast doubt on the forecasts made for the proposed new "Smart Car" being developed by Mercedes-Benz and Swiss watch company SMH. The vehicle will be a two-seat city car measuring just 2.5 metres in length. Micro Compact Car, the name given to the joint venture making the vehicle, predicted sales of 200,000 by the turn of the century. MarketScope said sales would not exceed 90,000 units by that date, and questioned MCC's pricing strategy for the new car.
-- BRANDS HATCH SETS SIGHTS ON 59 PERCENT RISE

Brands Hatch Leisure, which owns four motor racing circuits, is forecasting a rise of 59 percent in operating profits this year. The group is coming to market at the end of this month, and the profit forecast is contained in the pathfinder prospectus published Monday. It predicts that operating profits for the year to the end of December will be not less than 3 million sterling, compared to 1.88 million sterling for 1995.
-- PHARMA VISION BUYS 10 PERCENT OF US BIOTECH GROUP

U.S. biotechnology group Tularik, which develops oral drugs that regulate human gene behaviour, has raised $60 million via a private placement. The bulk of the funds for the unquoted group have been provided by Swiss investment fund Pharma Vision, which paid $33 million for a 10 percent stake in the group. San Francisco-based Tularik plans to go public next year.
